## Digital Marketing Agency in Pune: How to Do Keyword Research and Map Search Intent to Pages in 2026

Keyword research for a Pune service business is the work of finding the exact words your customers type, deciding what each of those searches is really asking for, and then assigning every search to one page on your website. A digital marketing agency in Pune that does this well hands you a map, not a list: one primary keyword per page, a stated intent for that page (learn, compare, buy, or find someone nearby), and a note on which pages must not compete with each other. The tools are mostly free and official: Google Search Console, Keyword Planner, your Google Business Profile performance data, a manual look at the results page, and the People Also Ask box. This guide shows how to use them in that order and how to turn the output into a page-by-page plan.

It is written for owners and marketing managers of Pune service businesses such as clinics, coaching classes and interior designers. The worked example is hypothetical: the business, the keywords and the numbers are illustrations, not data from any real client. We do not quote search volumes, because they differ by month and by tool, and you should read your own. Where we describe how Google's tools behave, we cite Google's own documentation, listed at the end.

### How this differs from other guides on this site

Our guide to [local SEO and the Google Map Pack in Pune](/blog/local-seo-google-map-pack-pune-2026) is about earning a place in the map results. A [content refresh and decay audit](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-seo-content-refresh-decay-audit-2026) is about fixing pages that have already lost traffic. Our piece on [AI Overviews and zero-click search](/blog/google-ai-overviews-digital-marketing-agency-pune-2026) covers a change in how results look. This article sits before all three: deciding what to write and which page should own which search, so that you are not repairing a muddled site later.

## Why keyword research is really about intent, not volume

A keyword is a clue to a need. Two searches can share the same words and want different things. Someone typing "interior designer" may be browsing ideas, and someone typing "interior designer near me" is probably ready to call. If you send both people to the same page, one of them leaves.

Google's own guidance on helpful content frames it the same way: content should be created primarily for people and not to manipulate search rankings. Among the warning signs it lists are covering many topics in the hope that some will rank, and targeting a word count because you believe Google prefers one. Keyword research that starts from the customer's question, rather than from a spreadsheet of volumes, stays on the right side of that line.

For a service business, four intents cover almost everything.

| Intent | What the searcher wants | Typical Pune example (illustrative) | Best page type |
|---|---|---|---|
| Informational | To understand or solve something | "how long does a kitchen renovation take" | Guide or blog article |
| Commercial | To compare options before choosing | "kitchen renovation contractor vs interior designer" | Comparison or "how to choose" page |
| Transactional | To hire or book now | "kitchen renovation quote" | Service page with enquiry form and call button |
| Local | Someone close by, now | "kitchen renovation in Kothrud" | Location page and Google Business Profile |

These categories overlap. "Digital marketing agency in Pune" is mostly commercial with a local edge. The results page shows which way a query leans.

## A five-step keyword research process

### Step 1: Start with what you already have in Google Search Console

If your site has been live for a few months, Search Console already holds the best keyword list you will ever get, because it records the real searches that showed your pages. Google's help documentation explains the basic route. In the Performance report, the Queries tab lets you sort by clicks, click-through rate or impressions, and the Pages tab does the same by URL. The table in the Pages tab is aggregated by page, so its totals can differ from the chart at the top.

Three habits make this useful for keyword mapping.

1. **Sort queries by impressions, not clicks.** Queries with many impressions and few clicks are searches where you appear but are not chosen. They often point to a page whose title or intent is slightly off.
2. **Click a query and open the Pages tab.** Google's help page notes that you can select a query and then check which of your URLs were shown for it. If two pages appear for the same query, you have found a possible cannibalisation problem, which we cover below.
3. **Use the branded and non-branded filter.** Search Console can separate queries that include your brand name from those that do not. Google notes this filter has data only from 11 March 2025 and is not available for sub-properties or sites with few impressions. Non-branded queries are the ones that show how strangers find you without already knowing your name.

Two cautions from Google's documentation. Query rows in the table are exact matches and are not case-sensitive, so use a regular expression filter when you want to group close variants such as "seo agency pune" and "seo company pune". And position is the topmost position of your link averaged across the queries where you appeared, so treat it as a direction, not a precise rank. Google's guidance is to look at trends in impressions and clicks rather than at position alone.

A new site will have little data. In that case, move on to the next steps and return to Search Console after two or three months.

### Step 2: Use Keyword Planner for ideas, with realistic expectations

Google Keyword Planner is part of Google Ads. Google describes it as a tool to research keywords for Search campaigns: you enter words or a website and get suggestions related to your products, services or website, along with estimates of how often a keyword is searched each month. Google's help page also says you must finish account setup, including billing information, to use basic features such as getting keyword ideas, so factor that into planning. You are not obliged to run ads to read the ideas, but check the current account requirements before promising a client anything.

What Keyword Planner is good for:

- **Vocabulary.** It shows the words real customers use. A Pune homeowner may search "flat interior" while your own page says "residential fit-out". The Google SEO starter guide makes the same point: users who know a topic well may use different terms than newcomers, so write with your readers' vocabulary in mind.
- **Relative size.** Use volume to compare two options, not as a forecast. A query with a few dozen monthly searches that is clearly transactional can be worth more than one with thousands that is informational.

### Step 3: Read your Google Business Profile search terms

If you serve customers in a specific part of Pune, your Business Profile performance data is a second source of real queries. Google's help page says the Searches metric shows the search terms people used to find your business, that it updates at the start of each month, and that it can take up to five days to appear. The same Performance view counts calls (clicks on the call button), direction requests and website clicks.

Two things to take from this:

- **Local-intent phrasing.** Terms such as "near me", an area name, or a landmark show how nearby customers describe where you are. Those words belong on your location pages and in your profile description, written naturally.

You cannot manage these queries directly; Google's page suggests improving your local ranking to appear for more of them. Google defines local ranking by relevance, distance and prominence, and notes that more reviews and positive ratings can help. For the practical side of that work, see our [Map Pack guide](/blog/local-seo-google-map-pack-pune-2026).

### Step 4: Inspect the results page yourself

This step costs nothing and is the one most often skipped. For each candidate keyword, search it in a private window, ideally with your location set to Pune, and look at what Google chooses to show. You are reading the results page as a statement of intent: Google has decided what people searching these words usually want, and it shows that.

Check these things and write them down.

- **What kinds of pages rank.** If the first page is mostly service pages from agencies, the intent is commercial or transactional. If it is mostly guides and explainers, a service page will struggle and a guide is the right format.
- **Is there a map pack?** A block of local businesses with a map signals local intent. A query whose results are mostly job listings and company-review sites is job-seeker intent, and ranking for it brings the wrong visitors even if the traffic looks good.
- **What features appear?** Videos, shopping results, news, or an AI-generated overview each change what a click is worth. See our note on [AI Overviews](/blog/google-ai-overviews-digital-marketing-agency-pune-2026).
- **How close are the titles to your idea?** If every result has "cost" or "price" in the title and your page does not discuss cost, you are answering a different question.

### Step 5: Mine People Also Ask and related searches

The People Also Ask box and the related searches at the bottom of the results page show how Google groups questions around a topic. Google does not publish a how-to for using them in keyword planning, so treat what follows as practical experience, not official guidance.

Use them for:

- **Supporting questions.** Questions that appear beneath a query are natural H2 or FAQ material on the page that owns that keyword. They tell you which sub-questions a good page should answer.
- **Gaps in your coverage.** If five related questions have no home on your site, you have either found an article to write or a section to add to an existing page.

Do not copy questions into a thin list of one-line answers. Google's guidance warns against summarising others' work without adding value, so answer from your own experience.

## The rule that keeps pages out of each other's way: one primary keyword per page

Once you have a list of keywords with an intent next to each, apply a simple rule: **every page gets one primary keyword and one intent, and every important keyword belongs to exactly one page.** Secondary keywords, the close variants and supporting questions, sit on the same page as natural language.

Why this matters: when two pages of your own target the same query with the same intent, Google has to pick one, and it may alternate between them. Google's site diversity documentation says that top results typically include no more than two listings from the same site, so a second page of yours is not guaranteed a slot, and it may push out a better page. Search Console will show the symptom: the same query returning two different URLs over time.

### How to spot cannibalisation

1. In the Performance report, filter to one query that matters.
2. Open the Pages tab and see whether more than one URL is listed.
3. Compare the two pages. If they answer the same question for the same reader, they compete. If one is a guide and the other a service page, they usually serve different intents and can coexist.

### How to fix it

- **Merge** two pages that say the same thing into the stronger one, and redirect the weaker URL. Google's SEO starter guide recommends redirecting non-preferred URLs to the best version, or specifying a canonical URL, to consolidate duplicates.
- **Re-point** one page to a different intent, such as turning a second "SEO services" page into "SEO audit: what you get".
- **Differentiate titles and headings.** Google asks for a distinct title that describes each page.

Distinct titles and meta descriptions are part of the same discipline. Google says descriptions should be unique and specific to each page and should summarise it, and that a keyword list is not a description. If a page's title does not suit the query, Google may write its own from headings or page text, so make the visible H1 clear too.

## A worked example (hypothetical): mapping keywords for a Pune home interior firm

Imagine a fictional business, "Sahyadri Interiors", a six-person home interior design firm in Pune with a studio in Baner. None of the details are real. The owner wants more consultation requests from homeowners in Baner, Aundh, Wakad and Hinjewadi.

After using the tools above, the agency produces this mapping. The keywords are illustrative.

| Page (URL) | Primary keyword | Intent | Secondary keywords on page | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| /interior-designer-pune | interior designer in Pune | Commercial, local | home interior designer Pune, interior design company | Main service page; results page shows agency and studio pages plus a map pack |
| /interior-design-baner | interior designer in Baner | Local, transactional | Baner flat interior, interior designer near Balewadi | Studio location page; matches Business Profile |
| /interior-design-wakad | interior designer in Wakad | Local, transactional | Wakad 2 BHK interior | Only if the firm really serves Wakad, with real projects described |
| /services/2-bhk-interior-design | 2 BHK interior design | Transactional | 2 BHK interior design packages, 2 BHK interior cost | Service page with scope and an enquiry form |
| /blog/interior-designer-cost-pune | interior design cost per sq ft Pune | Informational, commercial | what affects interior design cost | Guide; links to the 2 BHK page; ranges labelled as estimates |
| /blog/interior-designer-vs-contractor | interior designer vs contractor | Commercial | do I need an interior designer | Comparison for early shortlisters |
| /blog/modular-kitchen-planning | modular kitchen planning guide | Informational | kitchen layout, kitchen storage ideas | Top-of-funnel article |
| /contact-us | (none, brand and contact) | Navigational | Sahyadri Interiors Baner | Not a keyword target |

Three decisions worth noticing:

- **"Interior design cost" is kept off the service pages.** Both the cost article and the 2 BHK page could mention price. The article owns the cost question; the service page links to it and shows what is included. This stops them competing for the same query.
- **Location pages exist only where the firm has real presence.** A set of near-identical pages that only swap the area name would be a thin-content risk. Each location page needs genuinely different content, such as projects completed or building types worked in that area, and the firm's real address. If a firm has no Wakad projects, it does not get a Wakad page.
- **Each page's title is different.** For example: "Interior Designer in Baner, Pune: 2 and 3 BHK Homes" versus "2 BHK Interior Design in Pune: Scope and Process". The first is local, the second is a service, and the titles say so.

A few weeks after launch, the agency checks Search Console: for each primary keyword, does exactly one URL appear? If two do, it applies the fixes above.

## What this means for a digital marketing agency in Pune you are hiring

Hiring a digital marketing agency in Pune should include a clear deliverable for this work, usually before any content is written or any ads run. A good agency can give you the following, and you should ask for it in writing.

| Deliverable | What to look for |
|---|---|
| Keyword and intent map | A table like the one above: URL, primary keyword, intent, secondary terms |
| Evidence from your own data | Search Console queries and pages, Business Profile search terms, not only third-party volume figures |
| Results-page notes | Which features appear for each priority keyword, and why that decided the page type |
| Cannibalisation check | A list of any queries where two of your pages appear, with a merge, re-point or retitle decision |
| Page briefs | For each new page: the question it answers, headings, supporting questions, internal links |
| Title and description plan | Unique titles and descriptions per page, not a template repeated across the site |
| Reporting rhythm | A monthly review of queries and pages in Search Console against the map |

Warning signs: hundreds of keywords with no pages assigned, the same keyword given to several pages, a promised rank for a specific keyword, locality pages with only the name changed, and reports that show volume but not which page the traffic lands on. Our [guide to choosing a digital marketing agency in Pune](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-guide-2026) covers pricing and reporting in more detail.

## A simple checklist you can run yourself

- [ ] List the services you want enquiries for, in the words customers use.
- [ ] Pull queries and pages from Search Console; sort by impressions.
- [ ] Add ideas from Keyword Planner and from Business Profile search terms.
- [ ] Search each priority keyword and note what ranks and which features appear.
- [ ] Add supporting questions from People Also Ask and related searches.
- [ ] Assign one primary keyword and one intent to each page.
- [ ] Check no two pages share a primary keyword and intent.
- [ ] Write a unique title, H1 and meta description for each page.
- [ ] Review Search Console monthly and repeat the cannibalisation check.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is search intent in SEO?
Search intent is the reason behind a search: to learn something, compare options, buy or hire, or find something nearby. It decides what kind of page will satisfy the searcher. The results page is the best evidence, because it shows what Google has learned that people usually want for those words.

### How many keywords should one page target?
One primary keyword and one intent per page, plus a handful of close variants and supporting questions written naturally into the content. Chasing several unrelated keywords on one page usually dilutes it. If two keywords have different intents, they should have two pages.

### What is keyword cannibalisation and how do I find it?
It happens when two pages on your site compete for the same query with the same intent. In Search Console, filter the Performance report to a query and open the Pages tab; if two URLs are listed, compare them. Fix it by merging, re-pointing one page to a different intent, or retitling.

### Is Google Keyword Planner free to use?
Google's help page says you need to complete account setup, including billing information, to use basic features such as getting keyword ideas. That is separate from running ads. Check Google's current requirements, because account rules change.

### Do I need a separate page for every area of Pune?
No. Create a location page only where you have a real presence or a genuine service area, and give it unique content such as local projects. Near-identical pages that only change the area name add little value and can look like thin content.
